thread.text: is this the common way of doing this? can we make sure that this is the best way to do it

Hash routing is the standard pattern for exactly this shape of app: a single self-contained page whose server shouldn't own routes — docs viewers, GitHub-Pages SPAs, anything served from one static shell. The mainstream alternative, History-API *pathname* routing (`/flows/checkout.md`), is what product SPAs with routers use, but it needs the server to return the app shell for every deep path and to keep those paths from colliding with `/api` and `/auth` — server surface ReviewKit deliberately doesn't grow. Two smaller points in the hash's favor here: the fragment never reaches the server, so fact paths stay out of request logs; and it composes with the one-time-token auth redirect without extra rules. The trade-off is cosmetic (`#flows/checkout.md` vs `/flows/checkout.md`). If the viewer ever grows real server-rendered pages, pathname routing is the clean upgrade; for one page on loopback it would be added surface with no added capability.
